summary:
This autonomous health monitoring system allows astronauts to be medically independent during long duration deep space missions. It eliminates the need for astronauts to use medical spreadsheets by providing an engaging futuristic interface comprising of;

The Interactive 3D Digital Twin which is used to navigate the application. This is done through clicking on areas of the 3D mannequin to select different biological areas which are monitored to help astronauts understand dangers they face while in space. For example. This is further complimented by the colour coded health dashboard. To record new health concerns, astronauts can simply spin the mannequin to the correct area and click on it.

A gamified system which encourages astronauts to remain healthy by making it an essential part of their mission. This includes team based challenges to increase teamwork. Challenges include achieving a certain amount of deep sleep as a team which unlocks a reward for uploading to earth (e.g. Movie night). There is also a Resilience Skill Tree which allows astronauts to track their daily psychological and physical well-being.

This makes the application engaging and easy to use. It ensures crews remain physically and mentally well and mission ready.
details:
HealthSense is a 3D interactive web-based Digital Twin. Its purpose is to allow Astronauts to gain insight into the effects of protracted time spent in space. It centres around a 3D representation of the human body. Users can rotate this and select one of the 15 Body Areas (Head, Neck, Chest, Upper Spine, Lower Spine, Shoulder(s), Arm(s), Hip(s), Femur(s), Calf(s)) to display the relevant metrics. There are 3 Health Views available: Skeletal (Bone and Spine Load), Cardiovascular (Fluid Shifts and SANS Pressure) and Nervous (Cognitive and Radiation). All 15 Body Areas are assigned a colour: Cyan = Nominal, Amber = Caution or Red = Critical. Upon selecting a Body Area, a Card is displayed outlining a key message, summary and action plan for the astronaut. Some actions take several minutes e.g. 8 mins to relieve pressure across the Lower Spine, or 5 mins to restore joint movement in the Shoulder(s). Finally, the Astronaut can record any symptoms they are experiencing via the Logging tool, rating from 1-5 and providing further detail if required.

How it works

Data for all Body Areas and Health Views is pushed to the Telemetry API and persisted to the Central Store at a frequency of 2 seconds. A normalized score between 0-1 represents the 'risk' of each Body Area, with a corresponding Health Status applied (Caution if >0.4, Critical if >0.7). Each Body Area and Health View will show a title and summary. The 3D Application, Side Bar, Logging and Gamification modules do not communicate directly but instead access and update the Central Store. As such, the project can be split up between the development team.

Benefits

On future lunar and Martian expeditions, communication latency and limited access to medical professionals will be key challenges. HealthSense consolidates various measures of the Astronaut's physiological state into a single screen, allowing them to pinpoint problem areas and begin remedial measures. Through the inclusion of these longer-form mitigation plans and the ability to record symptoms, the Astronaut should be incentivized to perform the required actions to ensure the continued health of their skeletal, muscular, circulatory and cognitive systems.

Stack

We built the project using React 18, TypeScript and Vite. For the 3D element we leveraged Three.js (with react-three-fiber and drei) and used Zustand to store shared data. We wrote unit and integration tests using Vitest. A set of CSS variables provides consistent styling throughout and imparts a modern "glass" feel. Importantly, all incoming data originates from the TelemetrySource class. Therefore, the Telemetry Simulator can readily be replaced with a live connection to a WS or HTTP endpoint.

What was creative?

Instead of populating the screen with typical health monitoring screens, the Astronaut navigates the app using the 3D model. We added depth to the model and applied colour to the various Body Area layers to facilitate rapid comprehension. The codebase is structured to permit individual team members to focus on developing the 3D model, Side Bar, Logging or Gamification elements in parallel.

Limitations

A number of design decisions were taken to aid usability on an Astronaut's device. Touch targets are generous, the colour-coding of Body Area Health Status is prominent and the content on each screen is succinct. The 3D model and component rendering has also been streamlined to improve frame rate, via reduced polygon count and filtering. Due to the extensible architecture, additional Body Areas and data points can be incorporated with minimal changes. Obviously all figures shown are mock data, and no medical guidance has been used to inform the Body Area thresholds. HealthSense is currently only a proof-of-concept.
